    //==
    // The catalogs: each sum enumerated once, at the identity layer rather than
    // over meshes, so a caller can reach a name, a dual or a mesh from the same
    // array (`PlatonicSolid.All.Map(s => s.PolygonMesh3D)` for the meshes).

    // The five Platonic solids in ascending face count.
    All(_: PlatonicSolid): Array<PlatonicSolid>
        => [PlatonicSolid.Tetrahedron,
            PlatonicSolid.Cube,
            PlatonicSolid.Octahedron,
            PlatonicSolid.Dodecahedron,
            PlatonicSolid.Icosahedron];

    // The thirteen Archimedean solids, in the order of the sum declaration.

    //==
    // Meshes of the solid sums: the dispatch from each sum into the seed and

    // The five Platonic seeds are already projected onto the unit sphere, so
    // they pass through directly.
    PolygonMesh3D(s: PlatonicSolid): PolygonMesh3D
        => match (s) {

    //==
    // Placing a polyhedral solid needs no type of its own: the mesh is
    // transformable, so the placed form is
    // `PlatonicSolid.Icosahedron.PolygonMesh3D.ScaledAboutOrigin(r).TransformedByFrame(f)`.

    //==
    // Parametric builders: closed meshes for the prism, pyramid and antiprism
    // families. Rings walk counter-clockwise seen from +Z, caps and walls wind
    // counter-clockwise seen from outside
    // (Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - Winding, handedness, and normals).

    // The frame-local point at parameter t (in turns) around the Z axis at
    // radius `radius` and height `z`.
    RimPoint(t: Number, radius: Number, z: Number): Point3D
    {
        var p = PointOnCircle(t.Turns, radius);
        return (p.X, p.Y, z);
    }

    // Two SideCount-gon caps joined by SideCount rectangles: vertices 0..n-1
    // are the bottom ring at -Height/2, n..2n-1 the top ring at +Height/2.
    ToPolygonMesh(s: RegularPrism): PolygonMesh3D
    {
        var n = s.SideCount;
        var sides = n.ToNumber;
        var bottom = n.MapRange(i => RimPoint(i.ToNumber / sides, s.Radius, s.Height * -0.5));
        var top = n.MapRange(i => RimPoint(i.ToNumber / sides, s.Radius, s.Height * 0.5));
        var caps = Concatenate(Repeat(1, n.MapRange(i => n - 1 - i)),
                               Repeat(1, n.MapRange(i => n + i)));
        var walls = n.MapRange(i => [i, (i + 1) % n, n + ((i + 1) % n), n + i]);
        return PolygonMeshOfVertexNumbers(Concatenate(bottom, top), Concatenate(caps, walls))
            .TransformedByFrame(s.Frame);
    }

    // A SideCount-gon base at -Height/2 (vertices 0..n-1) tapering to the apex
    // (vertex n) at +Height/2 through SideCount triangles.
    ToPolygonMesh(s: RegularPyramid): PolygonMesh3D
    {
        var n = s.SideCount;
        var sides = n.ToNumber;
        var ring = n.MapRange(i => RimPoint(i.ToNumber / sides, s.Radius, s.Height * -0.5));
        var apex = Repeat(1, Point3D(0.0, 0.0, s.Height * 0.5));
        var cap = Repeat(1, n.MapRange(i => n - 1 - i));
        var walls = n.MapRange(i => [i, (i + 1) % n, n]);
        return PolygonMeshOfVertexNumbers(Concatenate(ring, apex), Concatenate(cap, walls))
            .TransformedByFrame(s.Frame);
    }
